narrator.name: The Atlas narrator
narrator.voice: warm, unhurried, curious; a documentary voice that never oversells; speaks the dance's own words (names, counts) clearly
narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language
narrator.wardrobe: in each episode the narrator wears the traditional apparel associated with the dance, reconstructed with meticulous care from the profile's costume notes and the licensed images — genuine and respectful, never a caricature; sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire is never worn (the narrator stays in neutral dress with a respectful nod in colour and fabric); the pack's visual_brief.wardrobe says which
narrator.languages: master narration in English; translations per language in episodes/i18n/<lang>/<slug>.json with the same scene structure (pipeline/translate.py); names, places and counts are never translated

instructor.persona: A local community leader or traditional dancer from Jujuy or Santa Cruz.

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The carnavalito is a pre-Hispanic dance of the Altiplano.
It evolved through syncretism with Spanish colonial culture.
In eastern Bolivia, it consolidated as a symbol of national integration after 1952.
on_screen: Map: Bolivia, Argentina, Chile, Peru · South America
Image — MISSING

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: It is performed during religious festivities and community celebrations.
It is a joyful, innocent, and communal activity, often serving as a game among participants.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Dancers move in rows, wheels, or serpentine lines.
A leader with a handkerchief directs the group.
Common figures include 'el puente' (the bridge), 'las alas' (the wings), and 'las calles' (the streets).
Watch for El puente, Las calles.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (2Ip3wl73Ld0)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Rows, wheels, and serpentine lines
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music is typically in a minor pentatonic mode.
Instruments include the quena, siku, charango, bombo, and caja chayera.
Listen for the quena, siku, charango, bombo.
The pulse is 3/4 in eastern variants; variable in Andean versions.
A blend of high-pitched Andean flutes (quena, siku) and the percussive, rhythmic strumming of the charango, creating a bright and communal atmosphere.

Form: Simple i-V harmony or minor pentatonic. Mood: joyful, festive, lively. It should sound like this: A blend of high-pitched Andean flutes (quena, siku) and the percussive, rhythmic strumming of the charango, creating a bright and communal atmosphere.
